events.title: Kickstarter campaign opens
events.summary: Avegant launched the Glyph Kickstarter campaign before I joined the company. Limit: Campaign launch, not funding close or product shipment. Credit: Avegant company milestone; this was before Erik’s arrival.
events.date_basis: Company campaign launch date, distinct from the February 21 funding close.

events.title: Kickstarter funding closes
events.summary: The Glyph Kickstarter campaign closed its funding period. Limit: Funding and backer counts do not establish the number of headsets shipped. Credit: Avegant company milestone; this was before Erik’s arrival.
events.date_basis: Dated company creator update; a funding milestone, not product delivery.

events.title: An established product architecture
events.summary: A HUGE design brief already described the headwear geometry, adjustment, folding, eye spacing and focus adjustments. This was part of the product context I inherited. Limit: This dates the brief, not Erik’s work or completion of the product. The January 2015 arm review is a separate later record. Credit: The brief names Bernhard Wildner as document owner. It predates Erik’s arrival.
events.date_basis: June 16 date printed on the brief cover; June 17 filename is not substituted. Later January 2015 material is excluded from this marker.

events.title: The original delivery estimate
events.summary: The hardware reward tiers originally estimated delivery in December 2014. Limit: An estimated month, not an actual shipment or an exact-day deadline. Credit: Avegant’s campaign commitment, made before Erik joined.
events.date_basis: Month-precision estimate attached to the original hardware rewards; no exact day is established.

events.title: Joining Avegant
events.summary: I joined Avegant as a Senior Mechanical Engineer to help get Glyph into production. Richard Lane recommended me to Joerg Tewes. That led to an introduction to Allan Evans. Limit: The actual start date is accepted recollection, corroborated by the intended date in the hiring correspondence. The offer alone does not prove attendance. Credit: Erik Norris; referral credit remains Richard Lane, Joerg Tewes and Allan Evans.
events.date_basis: Actual start date from Erik’s recollection; correspondence corroborates the intended date, rather than independently proving attendance.

events.title: Drawing notes released
events.summary: The revision history records the first release of the CAD drawing-notes document under my name. Limit: This is the document-release date. It does not date completion of company-wide adoption. Credit: Erik Norris is named on the document-release entry.
events.date_basis: August 10 document-release entry in the revision history. Broader rollout is not assigned this date.

events.title: Physical headstrap alternatives
events.summary: A dated concept deck records three physical headstrap mockups. Limit: The mockups are not proof of final selection or the production configuration. Credit: The deck does not establish sole authorship. The accepted account separately credits Radius’s support concepts and mockups.
events.date_basis: Date printed on the concept-deck cover; it dates the documented mockups, not final selection.

events.title: Refining the reliability methods
events.summary: My edited reliability plan addressed fixtures, actuation ranges, check intervals and environmental and drop-test methods, while asking colleagues to resolve missing conditions. Limit: The August 25 date comes from the edited-file identity. It is not the plan’s original date, protocol approval or a test pass. Credit: Frank Jiang authored the earlier plan. Erik’s edits request input from Jansen and Geoff.
events.date_basis: August 25 edited-file identity; displayed at month precision with no exact-day plot coordinate. Earlier Frank Jiang revisions remain separate.

events.title: Cosmetic criteria and inspection requirements
events.summary: I revised the general cosmetic and durability specification, adding cosmetic criteria and reorganizing the requirements for inspection, color measurement and supplier test reports. Limit: A specification revision, not proof that every prescribed test passed or every supplier accepted it. Credit: Billy Fung is credited for the initial requirements; Erik Norris is credited for revision 2.
events.date_basis: Native update-history row for revision 2; revision 1 dated 2015-07-24.

events.title: Coordinating supplier changes
events.summary: The EVT2 change tracker separated optics, headset and miscellaneous work and required supplier feasibility, cost and timing information followed by Avegant approval before tool changes. Limit: A record of change requests and approval steps, not a receipt that all changes were completed. Credit: A multi-person engineering and supplier workflow. Optics responsibilities remain with the named colleagues in the tracker.
events.date_basis: Tracker/deck date.

events.title: Ear-cover drawings revised
events.summary: Revision 7 ear-cover drawings recorded changes following the supplier reviews of ribs, shutoff draft and tool clearances. Limit: The drawing release does not prove the tools were modified or later samples passed. Intermediate revision dates are not made into a monotonic sequence. Credit: Supplier proposals and Erik’s written responses remain distinct from the original mechanical and drafting credits on the drawings.
events.date_basis: September 30 revision 7 entries only; earlier supplier agreement is background, not redated.

events.title: Custom engraving test instructions
events.summary: I specified a custom-engraving test batch and instructed the supplier to exclude the layout outline from the engraved artwork. Limit: A requested test batch, not proof of completion. The November 10 carrier and feed-hole request is a later action. Credit: Erik’s supplier instructions; supplier manufacture remains separately attributed.
events.date_basis: October 14 native slide date for the engraving request only; November 10 follow-up is excluded from this marker.

events.title: Liner material and marking revised
events.summary: The liner drawings removed an end-flange extension, changed the second-shot material and adjusted marking height. Limit: These are revised part definitions, not a claim that the material or appearance issues were resolved. November 18 work is not assigned to November 20. Credit: The November 20 revisions credit M. Young. Earlier November 18 clip and flange revisions credit L. Pang and M. Young.
events.date_basis: November 20 drawing revisions only; November 18 clip/flange changes remain earlier supporting context.

events.title: Inspection dimensions added
events.summary: I added inspection and critical-to-function dimensions to ear-cover and button-backer drawings without changing their 3D geometry. Limit: A drawing-control change, not proof of inspection execution or improved yield. Later exported note variants do not establish a single final policy. Credit: These revisions credit Erik. The underlying cover drawing retains C. Westra and C. Highnam’s original credits.
events.date_basis: Revision-table date on both December 3 and December 4 path instances; package dates are not new design-event dates.

events.title: Button-backer samples measured
events.summary: Received button-backer samples were checked against the specified contact feature following the earlier button-feel investigation and drawing change. Limit: November 30 dates the sample check, not the earlier investigation or revision. The measurements do not establish final button force or production acceptance. Credit: Erik prepared the investigation and is credited for the earlier backer revision. The parts were supplier samples.
events.date_basis: November 30 received-sample presentation/annotations only; November 9 investigation and November 12 revision are earlier actions.

events.title: Liner carrier drawings updated
events.summary: The liner carrier drawings incorporated Voke’s design-for-manufacture feedback. Limit: A dated drawing change. It does not prove adoption of PMP’s separate slide-removal proposal or stable production. Credit: The two revision-3 drawings separately credit E. Norris and M. Young.
events.date_basis: Revision 3 dates in December 8 exported drawing instances.

events.title: Shipping announced
events.summary: Avegant announced that Glyph shipping was beginning, with the first mailing expected late that week. Limit: An announcement, not independent verification of exact dispatch or customer receipt. Credit: Company-reported milestone; delivery depended on work across the company and its suppliers.
events.date_basis: Dated company creator update; the first mailing was still expected.

events.title: Tracking notices during the ramp
events.summary: Avegant reported sending more than 200 tracking numbers while the production line remained below full rate. Limit: Tracking notices are not customer receipts. Credit: Company-reported progress, not an individual engineering outcome.
events.date_basis: Dated company creator update; tracking notices are distinct from customer receipts.

events.title: Checking gloss variation
events.summary: Variation among production units prompted a request for matched-batch parts and quantified finish measurements. Limit: The marker dates the request. A later workbook is separate evidence; no acceptance band or elimination of variation is claimed. Credit: An engineering request to suppliers. Later measurements are supplier data, not sole personal test execution.
events.date_basis: February 10 request slide date only; later workbook date is not treated as the test date.

events.title: About 1,000 units reportedly shipped
events.summary: Avegant reported about 1,000 Glyph units shipped while international certification and order sequencing were still active. Limit: Preserve the approximation and attribution; this is not a verified customer-delivery count. Credit: Company-reported quantity.
events.date_basis: Dated company creator update; quantity remains approximate and company-reported.

events.title: Earpad gripper prototypes requested
events.summary: A dated presentation requested six earpad gripper prototypes. Limit: The date is printed inside the presentation despite an earlier filename. Separate acrylic grip tests are undated and do not become March 31 human-comfort results. Credit: The record documents the request without establishing sole concept authorship.
events.date_basis: March 31 date inside the prototype-request presentation; March 8 filename is not used. The separate grip workbook is undated.

events.title: Mechanical work continues through the ramp
events.summary: My weekly update still had cable-abrasion changes in validation, liner tooling and clamp-force work open, and sample and validation work underway with another cable supplier. Limit: A status snapshot. It does not close qualification, date a final configuration or turn future target dates into completed actions. Credit: Erik’s mechanical status report within continuing team and supplier work.
events.date_basis: Date of the weekly worksheet. Future target dates in its other columns are not completed event dates.

events.title: Kickstarter deployment reported complete
events.summary: Avegant reported that the Kickstarter units were fully deployed. Limit: This does not prove every customer’s receipt or satisfaction, or mark the end of engineering work. Credit: Company-reported milestone.
events.date_basis: Dated company creator update; deployment wording is not independently verified receipt or engineering closure.

events.title: A further clamp-force comparison
events.summary: A build-and-test matrix separated liner material, paint state and spring diameter, and required the parts and assembled units to be identified. Limit: A requested comparison, not a winning configuration or completed set of units. The preceding supplier correction to 70A stock and the next document’s 75A/70A ambiguity remain unresolved. Credit: Engineering test planning with supplier availability and material feedback from Nature.
events.date_basis: August 17 matrix/presentation date only. August 16 stock feedback is separately attributed context.

events.title: A liner tool change approved
events.summary: A response to the supplier’s liner-tool proposal records approval of a specific gate-area modification. Limit: Approval is visible in the August 25 response file. It does not prove the tool was changed, that flash was eliminated, or that a final material was selected. The August 24 investigation is a separate action. Credit: The supplier authored the proposal; Erik’s response file carries the approval.
events.date_basis: Approved overlay preserved in the August 25 response file; public display stays at month precision without an occurrence-day coordinate. August 24 diagnostic request is separate.

events.title: Leaving Avegant
events.summary: The accepted account recalls Chris Westra’s farewell as personal recognition of the work. Limit: This record does not establish a departure date or a first-generation engineering endpoint. Credit: Erik’s recollection of Chris Westra’s remarks.
events.date_basis: The recollection has no established date in this record.
